one_line: Compiles complex family hotel requirements into auditable multi-room stay plans.
what_it_does: Preserves a structured family brief, finds honest zero or multi-room results, and validates coverage, dates, price, and promotion scope before human review.
leverage_rationale: Structured shared state and deterministic validation materially improve an agent's ability to preserve children, room, and promotion constraints across staged checkout planning; generic UI driving would be error-prone.
leverage_evidence: Saved six-person brief preserves dates, ages, room limit, and constraints.
Split-checkout guardian verifies coverage, dates, $720, and room-only promotion scope.
Reload recomputes and restores the audit rather than losing state.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent, deliberately scoped review-only workflow with zero-result handling, preview plans, audit, acknowledgement, and receipt, but no submitted video and only packaging/claims limit observation.
execution_evidence: About text specifies end-to-end preview, guardian, reload, and review-only receipt behavior.
Demo is reported alive and public repository exists.
No video frame sheets submitted.
impact_rationale: Large families have a concrete, recurring planning problem that standard hotel search boxes handle poorly; preserving constraints and explaining promotion scope offers credible value.
impact_evidence: Specific six-person family scenario with one-room failure and two-room alternatives.
Addresses repeated re-entry, split searches, and promotion confusion.
creativity_rationale: The compiler and deterministic promotion guardian are a thoughtful interaction model for family travel rather than a generic booking form.
creativity_evidence: Honest zero-result plus constrained room-limit preview.
Review-only receipt records facts, unknowns, and guardian outcome.
usability_note: Constraint-preserving brief and explicit audit should reduce a difficult family-planning workflow; visual usability is not independently verifiable.
red_flags: No video evidence; visual claims cannot be checked.
advance_reason: Strong problem fit and unusually careful constraint/audit design, despite limited visual evidence.

one_line: Calculates landed import costs and compares sourcing origins through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Analyzes product, origin, quantity, and unit price for tariff rate, duty, landed cost, and margin impact, then reruns comparisons with another origin.
leverage_rationale: Typed tariff analysis and origin-switch tools give agents reliable parameterized calculations and shared live results, though the same narrow calculation is possible through a normal form or general agent with friction.
leverage_evidence: Two explicitly registered tools: analyze_tariff and switch_origin_country.
Tool invocation renders results on the same page as the human view.
execution_rationale: The app and narrow workflow are plausibly coherent, but there are no video frames, only one gallery image, and the packet does not establish calculation breadth or end-to-end reliability.
execution_evidence: React/Vite implementation and existing analysis functions are described.
Demo is reported alive and public repository exists.
No video frame sheets submitted and only one gallery image.
impact_rationale: Small importers have a concrete pre-purchase need for landed-cost and sourcing comparisons; the stated output directly addresses costly tariff surprises.
impact_evidence: Specific audience: small business owners importing goods.
Outputs duty and margin impact before purchase order and compares origin savings.
creativity_rationale: Useful agent-connected tariff calculator with live shared rendering, but the underlying product concept is a familiar calculator/comparison tool.
creativity_evidence: Origin switching preserves prior shipment context.
WebMCP results are visible in the existing analysis UI.
usability_note: Narrow inputs and origin comparison appear straightforward; visual evidence is thin.
red_flags: No video frames; only one gallery image.
Accuracy and tariff-data provenance are not evidenced in the packet.
advance_reason: Clear niche value, but limited evidence and modest novelty make it weaker than the strongest packets.

one_line: Turns an ordinary-language home repair description into a routed, reviewable quote brief.
what_it_does: Matches a homeowner's unchanged request to one of 222 routes, infers only relevant facts, separates multiple jobs, and gates finalisation behind explicit permission.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides structured routing, fact visibility, permission gating, and server validation that are materially safer and more reliable than an agent clicking a generic trades quote flow.
leverage_evidence: Agent matches to exact route among 222 published routes.
Two independent jobs remain two briefs and final tool is unavailable until permission.
Server-validated receipt avoids creating a live lead.
execution_rationale: A 178-second demo is present and the described central workflow covers routing, inference, review, permission, and test receipt coherently.
execution_evidence: Video exists with 178-second titled demo.
Description specifies visible provided/inferred facts, missing gates, and final receipt.
Demo is alive and repository is public.
impact_rationale: Homeowners commonly know the problem but not the trade; reducing routing and quote-request friction is a credible practical benefit.
impact_evidence: Examples include muddy lawn, leaking appliance, crumbling step, and extractor opening.
Targets matching ordinary-language needs to appropriate trade services.
creativity_rationale: The combination of semantic service routing, progressive safe tools, and explicit permission is a fresh synthesis for quote requests.
creativity_evidence: Read-only semantic recovery records why it selected Builders.
Separate permission and finalisation gates are part of the interaction model.
usability_note: Starts with natural language and exposes inferred facts before submission, supporting understandable review.
red_flags: Final live lead creation is not demonstrated; receipt is a test receipt.
advance_reason: Strong evidence-backed workflow and meaningful agent advantage for a real homeowner problem.

one_line: Coordinates one urgent family story across four fictional essential-service providers.
what_it_does: Projects one story into planning constraints, checks eligibility and schedule conflicts, minimizes disclosures, blocks unjustified ID requests, and stages a human-approved plan.
leverage_rationale: The shared story, cross-service coordination, disclosure accounting, deterministic eligibility, and human authority are precisely the sort of multi-site state an agent cannot reliably reproduce by generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: One story is staged across four coordinated services.
Two schedule conflicts avoided and unjustified Government ID request blocked.
Zero applications sent before approval; visible outcome rail preserves authority.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent working demonstration and detailed safety contract, but the demo link is dead and no video transcript is available; frame claims cannot be checked.
execution_evidence: About text reports four staged services, eligibility checks, conflict avoidance, and approval gate.
Demo is reported dead and gallery_images=0.
No independent visual packaging beyond screenshot is usable as runtime proof.
impact_rationale: Families facing an urgent unsafe-home event have a high-stakes, specific need where repeated storytelling, conflicts, and excessive disclosure create real harm.
impact_evidence: Concrete scenario: unsafe home, three children, shelter, food, health check, accessible transport within 72 hours.
Design directly addresses repeated forms, appointment collisions, and unnecessary sensitive data.
creativity_rationale: Tell-once coordination with purpose-bound disclosure and human-controlled staging is an ambitious and memorable service interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Four-service coordination from one story.
Blocks unjustified ID request and keeps final authority with the person.
usability_note: Outcome rail and explicit approvals suggest strong transparency, but runtime cannot be checked.
red_flags: No gallery images and no video transcript; fictional providers limit real-world validation.
standouts: Cross-service conflict avoidance with human approval.
advance_reason: Exceptional concept and impact potential merit advancement, but runtime eligibility needs verification.

one_line: Lets a human and AI draw, edit, and continue on one shared editable canvas.
what_it_does: Provides drawing, writing, selection, and AI Pen interactions so an agent can explain or improve visual work while retaining editable shared state.
leverage_rationale: Shared canvas state and editable continuation are meaningfully better than an agent describing UI clicks, especially for spatial drawing and iterative correction.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly describes human edits followed by agent continuation.
Gallery captions claim agent-created Mona Lisa, neural network, and HTTP explanations.
Canvas artifacts remain editable.
execution_rationale: The concept and sample outputs are coherent, but no video frames were submitted and the packet gives little evidence of robust selection/continuation behavior.
execution_evidence: Multiple described/gallery examples cover art and educational diagrams.
Demo is reported alive and repository is public.
No video frame sheets submitted.
impact_rationale: Students and learners can benefit from visual explanations that are editable and interactive rather than text-only.
impact_evidence: Inspiration identifies difficult school topics and direct whiteboard explanation.
Supports diagrams, arrows, notes, and iterative correction.
creativity_rationale: Shared human-agent drawing with continuation from human edits is a compelling interaction, though whiteboard-plus-AI is an established direction.
creativity_evidence: AI Pen supports pointing/selecting regions.
Agent can continue from human-modified canvas rather than regenerate a static result.
usability_note: Editable canvas and direct visual interaction are promising; runtime evidence is limited.
red_flags: Agent quality and shared-state reliability are asserted rather than demonstrated end-to-end.
advance_reason: Good interaction idea, but evidence is too thin and differentiation is moderate.

one_line: A browser parametric cabinet studio that turns spatial designs into validated cut and CNC outputs.
what_it_does: Models cabinetry in 3D, validates clearances and NKBA constraints, nests panels, and exports DXFs and assembly guides with agent parity.
leverage_rationale: Agents need structured spatial state, validation, undo, nesting, and machine-output operations; generic browser driving would be substantially less reliable for parametric geometry and production constraints.
leverage_evidence: 26 strict-schema WebMCP tools expose design, inspection, and undo.
Exact 3D model shared by human and agent.
Validation and CNC-ready outputs are structured downstream consequences.
execution_rationale: The packet presents unusually detailed geometry, validation, nesting, and export scope with video frame sheets and a live demo, though transcript is absent.
execution_evidence: Detailed integer-sixteenths geometry and rotation formulas.
Claims live clash validation, sheet nesting, layered DXF, and assembly export.
Demo alive, public repo, and three frame sheets submitted.
impact_rationale: Small cabinet shops and woodworkers have a concrete need for affordable browser-based design-to-fabrication tooling; the claimed outputs directly address it.
impact_evidence: Targets gap between expensive desktop cabinet software and generic 3D tools.
Produces cut lists, nesting, DXF layers, and assembly guides.
creativity_rationale: The combination of agent-native spatial CAD, woodworking-specific validation, and fabrication outputs is ambitious and unusually specific.
creativity_evidence: NKBA and physical clash validation in a browser studio.
Edge-band and kerf-aware guillotine nesting with CNC layers.
usability_note: Domain-specific constraints can make a complex workflow practical, though visual inspection is unavailable.
red_flags: Transcript absent; exact production correctness is not independently verified.
advance_reason: High leverage and originality with substantive technical scope and video evidence.

one_line: A control room that diagnoses failed agent jobs, preserves checkpoints, and resumes them with approval.
what_it_does: Uses WebMCP to inspect failures, compare providers, preserve completed work, require human approval, recover from checkpoints, and verify completion.
leverage_rationale: The product's purpose is structured agent workflow state and recovery; live checkpoint, provider, audit, and approval operations are not comparably reliable through UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Seven tools diagnose, compare, recover, and verify jobs.
HTTP 429 at 73% is preserved and Provider Beta resumes from checkpoint.
Human approval gates provider switching.
execution_rationale: Claims a coherent recovery workflow with strong packaging evidence, but no video frame sheets were submitted, so execution remains claimed rather than observed.
execution_evidence: Gallery captions describe failure, checkpoint, approval, external bridge proof, and 100% recovery.
Demo alive and repository public.
No video frame sheets submitted.
impact_rationale: Agent builders and operators have a real reliability problem when provider failures lose partial work; checkpointed recovery and approvals offer direct operational value.
impact_evidence: Concrete HTTP 429 failure scenario at 73% progress.
Preserves completed work and verifies resumed completion.
creativity_rationale: Treating failure recovery and human-controlled provider substitution as a first-class agent product is a strong, memorable systems concept.
creativity_evidence: Recovery control room rather than only monitoring.
Audit trail plus approval before consequential provider switch.
usability_note: Operational outcome rail and explicit approval should support safe recovery; visual runtime check unavailable.
red_flags: No video frame sheets; gallery claims are packaging evidence rather than runtime proof.
standouts: Human approval and external-agent bridge proof.
advance_reason: High-value agent-infrastructure problem with a strong recovery interaction and credible evidence claims.

one_line: An adaptive blog and reading platform whose agent reshapes interface and drafts around the reader.
what_it_does: Offers personalization of layout, typography, colors, reading modes, voice guidance, publishing, profiles, and a 44-tool WebMCP inspector.
leverage_rationale: Agents can manipulate many structured presentation and writing settings in shared state, but much of the outcome is achievable through UI controls or browser automation; WebMCP is meaningful rather than indispensable.
leverage_evidence: 44 tools expose schemas and live execution in-page.
Agent can reshape density, measure, type scale, surfaces, palettes, and drafts.
Publishing composer exposes structured fields to agents.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a broad, coherent prototype with numerous named surfaces and three frame sheets, but no transcript and no repository reduce certainty about completeness.
execution_evidence: Nine gallery images and three video frame sheets are listed.
Demo alive; project is presented as a prototype.
Named reading, personalization, voice, telemetry, composer, and profile surfaces.
impact_rationale: Readers and writers with strong accessibility or preference needs can benefit from adaptive presentation and agent-assisted publishing, though the problem is less acute than core workflow submissions.
impact_evidence: Targets reader/writer customization and distraction-free reading.
Supports layout, type, color, and drafting preferences.
creativity_rationale: Treating the interface itself as agent-reconfigurable, including reading modes and personalization telemetry, is a fresh synthesis pursued across many surfaces.
creativity_evidence: Adaptive desk and voice guide connect spoken intent to WebMCP actions.
Warm-paper reading mode and OLED mode are part of a configurable product state.
usability_note: Rich customization may serve preference-driven readers, but breadth risks complexity; visual evidence was not independently available.
red_flags: Broad prototype scope may leave depth/completeness uncertain.
standouts: Large in-page tool inspector and multiple reading modes.
advance_reason: Interesting adaptive-interface concept, but evidence and repository transparency are weaker than competing entries.

one_line: A browser modular synth where human and agent patch one live, lockable Web Audio graph.
what_it_does: Lets an agent inspect, create, remove, connect, disconnect, and tune synth modules while humans lock parameters and observe shared live audio state.
leverage_rationale: Typed access to live graph topology, parameters, locks, and spectrum gives agents precise spatial/audio control that general UI driving cannot reliably provide; human and agent share one instrument state.
leverage_evidence: Agent operates the same live Web Audio graph as the human.
Tools cover graph inspection, module lifecycle, patching, parameters, and spectrum.
Hand-locked parameters are enforced as boundaries.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent synth with live graph, lock semantics, self-testing, and WebMCP verification; three frame sheets and a live demo support the claim, though no transcript is provided.
execution_evidence: Gallery claims startup synth, live agent message, tool verification, and lock confirmation.
Demo alive and public repository exists.
Three video frame sheets submitted.
impact_rationale: Electronic musicians and sound-design learners have a credible desire for steerable collaborative patching rather than opaque generated audio.
impact_evidence: Addresses common limitation of static or hidden AI sound generation.
Supports modular synthesis, sequencing, effects, spectrum reading, and human steering.
creativity_rationale: A live collaborative instrument with enforceable human ownership boundaries is a novel interaction model, not merely chat-to-audio generation.
creativity_evidence: Human locks survive agent operations as enforced boundaries.
Agent patches the graph while the human edits the same instrument.
usability_note: Shared graph and locks support understandable collaboration, but modular synthesis remains intrinsically complex.
red_flags: Bring-your-own API key may add setup friction.
Audio quality and full graph correctness are not independently measured.
standouts: True shared live Web Audio graph.
advance_reason: Exceptionally strong WebMCP fit and original human-agent creative interaction, with substantial evidence.

one_line: Builds personalized learning plans by searching and comparing resources against a learner's constraints.
what_it_does: Uses learner knowledge, time, budget, and language to search, compare, and assemble a trustworthy path toward a large learning goal.
leverage_rationale: Structured agent interaction can preserve learner constraints and assemble a plan across resources, but a general agent can perform much of this research with friction; WebMCP's delta is meaningful, not transformative.
leverage_evidence: Pitch names knowledge, time, budget, and language as structured inputs.
Workflow searches, compares, and builds a path together.
Project explicitly pivots from a more complex workshop coordination concept.
execution_rationale: The product rationale is coherent and a three-sheet video packet is listed, but only one gallery image and no transcript limit verification of the central plan-building flow.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive and public repository exists.
Three video frame sheets submitted.
About text states search, comparison, and plan construction but provides limited concrete completion evidence.
impact_rationale: Learners changing careers or developing skills face a real problem of sequencing resources around prior knowledge, time, budget, and language.
impact_evidence: Concrete examples include new photographers seeking professional work.
Addresses fragmented search and manual plan rebuilding.
creativity_rationale: Constraint-aware, agent-assisted learning-path construction is a useful fresh synthesis, though learning roadmaps are a familiar category.
creativity_evidence: Combines learner profile constraints with resource comparison.
Concept evolved from user testing of an overcomplicated workshop product.
usability_note: Constraint inputs promise personalization, but evidence does not show how plans are presented or revised.
red_flags: Only one gallery image and no transcript.
Resource quality and plan evaluation are not evidenced.
standouts: Explicit product simplification after user testing.
advance_reason: Clear audience and useful concept, but execution and WebMCP differentiation are insufficiently evidenced relative to stronger projects.
